Paste raw SVG code or SVG path d data. Curves are rasterized into a high-res spray mask template.
Wraps the active layer 50% horizontally and vertically, moving its edges to the center where they're easy to see and paint over. This softens that seam — it won't fully fix it on its own, but gives you a much easier starting point.
Quantizes the active layer's colors down to at most this many, picking the best-fitting set automatically (median cut) and remapping every pixel to its nearest match. Useful after loading a photo or a JPEG-compressed image, which often has thousands of nearly-identical colors from compression artifacts even when it looks flat.
Pick colors to protect from merging (weight above 1x) or reduce more aggressively (below 1x). Also affects similar nearby colors, not just the exact shade picked.
How far a weighted color's influence reaches — low means only near-identical shades are affected, high spreads the effect across a broader range of similar colors.
Groups similar colors together and picks ONE existing color from each group to represent it everywhere — never blends or invents a new color, only ever keeps colors already in the image.
Tolerance sets how wide a hue range gets grouped together — low keeps fine distinctions, high consolidates more aggressively. Curve picks where in that range the kept color comes from (50 = the middle; push toward 0 or 100 to favor one end).
E.g. push Luminance Curve toward 100 to favor keeping the lighter shade from each group instead of the middle one.
0% leaves hues untouched; 100% fully converts every color to the target hue. Pick a warm color to warm the palette, a cool one to cool it.
Negative mutes toward gray; positive pushes toward more vivid.
Negative darkens toward black; positive lightens toward white.
Reducing first means the image and the extracted palette match exactly.
🎨 Color Picker
Click a swatch to lock it in (circle) or unlock it (square) — locked colors influence what Regenerate produces. Drag swatches to reorder before regenerating.
How many swatches away a locked color's influence reaches. Beyond that distance, an unlocked swatch isn't influenced by it at all.
How much color variation gets applied around whichever locked color is influencing a swatch — low stays close to it, high explores further.
When a swatch is too far from any locked color for Spread to reach it, it leans toward this relationship to a locked color's hue instead of a fully random one. Hover an option above for a description.
Snaps each block of pixels to its single most common color, removing blur/antialiasing left from scaling or export. Grid Size is how many pixels wide/tall one "true" pixel is in this image.
If the auto-detected grid looks shifted from the actual pixel edges, nudge these until it lines up.
Stretches everything to the new size, keeping hard pixel edges instead of blurring.
When content isn't scaled, this is where the existing content sits within the new canvas.
Pixel-perfect (nearest-neighbor) — hard edges, no blur. Scales from the selection's top-left corner.

Seamless

Shows everything currently visible, tiled 3×3 with the real thing in the center, so you can check if the edges line up seamlessly as you paint.

Tool Settings

Anchor: None (Alt+Click on canvas or use button)

Grid

Uses the first grid in the list above — add one to enable snapping.

Shortcuts

B / S / E / G / H / M / R — switch tool (G for Path)
[ ] — brush size down/up
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z — undo/redo
Wheel — zoom (centered on cursor) · 0 — fit · 1 — 100%
Middle-click drag / Space-drag — pan
Ctrl+click swatch — add/remove from spray selection
Shift+click swatch — select range
Ctrl+S — export PNG
